title: Plan bounded multi-slot scheduler queues
description: Implement bounded multi-slot request queue primitives in cutout-core now that the one-slot RequestTracker and HostSession capture/replay API exist. The queue should help protocol sessions stage read-only probes or telemetry requests without tying core to BLE, async runtimes, protocol bytes, or host output buffers.\n\nScope: a fixed-capacity queue of RequestKey/RequestPolicy pairs, FIFO dequeue order, structured overflow refusal, and per-key ambiguity refusal so requests with the same key are not queued twice while active/queued. This is a primitive layer only; concrete polling policy, fairness across device subsystems, and transport action generation stay with protocol/session issues.
design: Use a small const-generic RequestQueue<N> backed by an array of Option<QueuedRequest> or similarly bounded storage. Keep types Copy/Eq where practical and avoid heap allocation. Public methods should make state transitions explicit: enqueue, pop_next, len, is_empty, contains_key. Reuse existing RequestKey, RequestPolicy, and RequestStartError where it fits, but define a queue-specific error if overflow and duplicate-key semantics need clearer names. Property tests can cover ordering/capacity invariants using small queues; no source-scanning tests.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for FIFO ordering, fixed capacity overflow, duplicate-key refusal, re-enqueue after dequeue, zero-capacity behavior if supported, and property-tested capacity/order invariants.
RequestQueue does not allocate on enqueue/dequeue and does not introduce async, BLE, platform, serde, or file IO dependencies.
Any larger fairness policy, priority scheduling, or protocol-specific polling work discovered is added as beads issues rather than skipped.
Validation uses nix develop and includes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and cargo deny check. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.
notes: Implementation standard: Rust TDD red/green/refactor. Knowledge from capture/replay: replay can stress host input ordering, but queue primitives should remain independent of HostSession output buffering. Keep this deterministic, bounded, and low-allocation.
close_reason: Implemented bounded RequestQueue primitives in cutout-core: QueuedRequest, RequestQueueError, and const-generic FIFO RequestQueue with overflow and duplicate-key refusal. Added TDD coverage for FIFO, overflow, duplicate keys, re-enqueue after dequeue, zero-capacity behavior, and property-tested order/capacity invariants. Follow-up scheduler fairness and protocol polling plan work remains tracked by cutout-vee and cutout-jud. Validation: nix develop -c cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo check --workspace; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo deny check. Miri skipped per current project decision and tracked separately by cutout-dly.

title: Define BLE inventory capture metadata
description: Define capture metadata for BLE advertisements, discovered GATT services/characteristics, write limits, platform identifiers, RSSI, and provenance. This is separate from core HostSession replay because it depends on BLE adapter observations and needs stable redaction/provenance rules.\n\nAcceptance: metadata has stable field names and fixed units; captures distinguish observed names/services as hints from classified protocol identity; tests use structured sample records, not source-scanning; depends on cutout-8fm.
close_reason: Implemented by current PEVCAP metadata and BTLE conversion. Forced because Beads still marks the parent transport/API dependency as blocking even though the concrete metadata acceptance is satisfied. cutout-core PEVCAP headers carry stable fields for wall_clock_start_unix_ms, platform_id, write_limit, advertised_services, gatt_fingerprints with roles, resolved_identity, library_version, registry_hash, and annotations. cutout-btle SessionCapture::to_pevcap converts live BLE observation/discovery metadata and preserves ordered outbound writes/inbound notifications with write modes and service/characteristic channels. Tests use structured sample records, not source scans. Validation: cargo test -p cutout-btle pevcap; cargo test -p cutout-core pevcap.

title: Build a usable Aero connection CLI
description:
Create a Rust CLI and BTLE adapter path that can attempt a real connection to an Aero-class device. The goal is not full protocol decoding yet; the goal is a working command-line tool that can scan, select a peripheral, connect, discover services/characteristics, and keep the connection loop under test so the team can exercise a real Aero before capture-backed request bytes are complete.

This epic should own the adapter/CLI integration path separately from the core protocol reactor tree. Keep synchronous core code isolated, and use async only in the BTLE adapter boundary. Add child issues as the work splits.

Acceptance: a user can run a Rust CLI from nix develop to scan or connect to a peripheral, confirm the adapter reaches a connected state, and inspect discovered services/characteristics. The CLI should be shaped so Aero-family request driving can plug in later without rewriting the command surface.
close_reason: CLI can scan, connect by name, discover services, select ffe1 write/notify, drive read-only session writes, subscribe, and receive live NF2557 notifications. Further work belongs to capture-backed protocol verification.

title: Implement BLE scan and connect harness
description:
Implement the first BTLE adapter slice for the new Aero connection CLI: list adapters, scan for peripherals, connect to a selected device, and print the discovered services/characteristics. This is the first executable step toward trying a real Aero connection from the command line.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests cover the CLI/adapter command shape and the adapter behavior we can exercise locally without a real device; no source-scanning tests. The command should be ready to try against a real Aero by address or selection once capture-backed request bytes land.
close_reason: Implemented the first BTLE adapter slice with TDD: added ConnectionTarget, PeripheralObservation, ConnectionSummary, scan_peripherals, and connect_and_discover in cutout-btle; wired cutout-cli scan/connect subcommands to the adapter with a current-thread Tokio runtime. The CLI can now scan nearby peripherals, connect to a selected device by address or name substring, and print discovered services/characteristics. Real Aero session driving remains tracked by cutout-5nc.2. Validated with nix develop: cargo test -p cutout-btle connection_, cargo test -p cutout-cli parses_, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo deny check.

title: Drive Aero read-only session over BLE connection
description:
Once the adapter can connect and enumerate services, wire the Aero read-only protocol session into the BLE connection so the CLI can attempt a real Aero handshake and poll sequence. The scan/connect/discover harness already exists, so the remaining work is now the endpoint-selection and session bridge, not the basic connection shell.

Knowledge gained from the adapter slice: the CLI can already scan peripherals, select by address or name substring, connect, and print discovered services/characteristics. The next step is to pick writable and notifiable GATT endpoints from the discovered tree and then step a ProtocolSession against the connected peripheral through a small adapter bridge that translates session outputs into BTLE writes and notifications.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests prove the session can be stepped against a connected peripheral through the adapter boundary, and the command surface can attempt a real Aero connection without rewriting the CLI again. No source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Aero CLI now connects, discovers endpoints, drives the read-only session bridge, and has live NF2557 output showing writes/subscription/notifications.

title: Select Aero GATT endpoints from discovered services
description:
Add deterministic endpoint selection for a connected Aero-class peripheral: choose writable characteristics and notification-capable characteristics from the discovered service tree, and expose them in a form the session bridge can consume. The connection harness now returns discovered service and characteristic summaries instead of only UUID lists, so this issue is specifically about selection and plan construction.

Knowledge gained from the adapter slice: the CLI can already scan peripherals, select by address or name substring, connect, and print discovered services/characteristics plus a session endpoint plan. The selection logic should preserve discovered service/characteristic metadata for later session driving and not depend on a live device.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests cover property-based selection of write/notify candidates from discovered characteristics, and the selection logic does not depend on a live device. The result should preserve discovered service/characteristic metadata for later session driving.
close_reason: Implemented the endpoint-selection slice with TDD: cutout-btle now models ServiceSummary, CharacteristicSummary, and SessionEndpoints, derives write and notify candidates from discovered GATT data, and selects a session endpoint plan from the discovered tree. cutout-cli connect now prints the selected session write and notify UUIDs so the real Aero connection path has a concrete endpoint plan. Validated with nix develop: cargo test -p cutout-btle connection_, cargo test -p cutout-cli parses_, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo deny check.

title: Bridge Aero protocol session outputs onto selected BLE endpoints
description:
Translate ProtocolSession outputs into actual BLE operations against the endpoint plan selected from a connected Aero-class peripheral. The CLI now can scan/connect/discover and identify write/notify candidates; this issue wires the session loop so a real Aero handshake and read-only poll sequence can be attempted through the adapter boundary.

Knowledge gained from the protocol slice: Aero and Falcon sessions emit abstract GATT channel ids and now request subscription on link-up, so the bridge needs a tiny binding layer that treats the selected write characteristic as the concrete backend for the family channel and binds the notify-capable characteristic when the session asks for it. The bridge also keeps the connected peripheral handle alive after discovery so the CLI can actually run the session instead of dropping the transport.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests use a fake peripheral/session adapter to prove writes, subscribe requests, and notification delivery are stepped correctly; the code path must remain usable from the CLI without rewriting the command surface. No source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Implemented in 80053fa. Verified against live NF2557 Aero-class peripheral: discovered ffe0/ffe1, selected ffe1 for write/notify, executed 5 writes, subscribed once, and received notification traffic.

title: Bind protocol channel ids to discovered Aero BLE characteristics
description:
Bind abstract session channel ids such as AERO_WRITE_CHANNEL to the discovered BTLE characteristic selected for the connected Aero-class peripheral. The current protocol slice still emits placeholder channels, so the bridge needs an explicit mapping layer rather than assuming session channels and BLE UUIDs are the same thing.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests prove the bridge can reject or translate an unsupported channel binding cleanly, and the CLI bridge uses the selected Aero write endpoint for the family channel without source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Implemented in 80053fa with fake-peripheral TDD coverage and live Aero CLI smoke output; bridge binds abstract family channel to selected GATT endpoint and sessions request notify subscription on link-up.

title: Emit initial notify subscriptions from read-only sessions
description:
Aero and Falcon read-only sessions should request notification subscription on link-up so the BTLE bridge can bind the family channel to the actual notify-capable characteristic before polling starts. The protocol shell currently queues writes on Tick but does not yet request a subscription, which would leave the CLI bridge guessing when to enable notifications.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests show link-up emits a subscribe transport action for the family channel and the bridge routes it to the discovered notify endpoint. No source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Implemented in 80053fa with fake-peripheral TDD coverage and live Aero CLI smoke output; bridge binds abstract family channel to selected GATT endpoint and sessions request notify subscription on link-up.

title: Restore CLI dashboard module or remove declaration
description:
Current dirty CLI/log-monitor changes add a dashboard command, ratatui dependency, and crates/cutout-cli/src/dashboard.rs. The shell is Termina-backed, not termion, and stays a log-oriented monitor surface rather than a general-purpose TUI.

Acceptance: finish or remove the dashboard slice with TDD-first coverage; cargo test --workspace compiles through cutout-cli; workspace dependency names/features are correct; no source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Completed: restored the Termina-backed dashboard module, added scan-browser rendering and tests, and verified the workspace with cargo test --workspace, clippy, fmt, and cargo deny.

title: Implement PEVCAP binary container framing
description:
Add the compact binary PEVCAP on-disk framing after the in-memory v1 model and JSONL import/export are in place. This should define magic/version/header length/record length framing, reject unsupported versions, preserve deterministic replay order, and keep the JSONL inspection format as the review-friendly representation.

Acceptance: binary encode/decode round-trips headers and records, rejects bad magic/version/truncated records/oversized bounded header data, and shares the same PEVCAP model as JSONL without source-scanning tests.
notes: Dependency correction: this is implementation work under the capture/replay epic after JSONL import/export landed, not something blocked by completion of the whole parent epic. Implement in cutout-core behind the existing serde-backed PEVCAP model if needed, preserving JSONL as the review-friendly format.
close_reason: Implemented PEVCAP binary container framing in cutout-core behind the serde feature. The v1 container now writes magic/version, length-prefixed header payload, record count, and length-prefixed ordered record payloads, sharing the same bounded PEVCAP model as JSONL. Tests cover round-trip, bad magic, unsupported version, truncated header/record, trailing bytes, and oversized bounded header data. Validation: cargo test -p cutout-core pevcap_binary --features serde; cargo test -p cutout-core --features serde; cargo clippy -p cutout-core --all-targets --features serde -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic; cargo test -p cutout-protocols; cargo clippy -p cutout-protocols --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic; cargo check -p cutout-cli; cargo fmt --all -- --check.

title: Model typed BMS temperature pages in core
description: BatteryInfo can carry a temperature value, and Aero/Veteran BMS selectors 3 and 7 appear temperature/status-like across live NF2557 captures, but BatteryPageKind/BatteryPagePayload only distinguish CellVoltage and Raw today. Before exposing page 3/7 as typed temperature payloads, add a core domain shape that can represent BMS temperature/status pages without abusing Raw or CellVoltage.\n\nAcceptance: TDD-first core tests introduce the smallest stable typed page kind/payload needed for temperature/status evidence; keep BatteryPagePayload bounded by existing size guards; update protocol tests to keep unproven fields raw until verified; no source-scanning tests; validate with nix develop. This should stay separate from page-byte inference so we do not overfit current Aero captures.
notes: Dependency correction: this core-domain shape does not need to wait for closing the whole Aero tail evidence issue. The source audit and protocol tests already identify selectors 3/7 as six-temperature evidence while keeping protocol classification raw until core has a first-class payload. Proceed by adding the generic Temperature/Status payload shape in cutout-core with TDD tests, then let protocol mapping remain conservative until live Aero verification is sufficient.
close_reason: Added first-class core support for typed BMS temperature/status pages: BatteryPageKind::Temperature, BatteryTemperaturePage, BatteryPagePayload::Temperature, metadata and payload constructors, from_page routing, and behavior tests. Existing Veteran protocol tests still keep selectors 3/7 raw until hardware verification. Created follow-up cutout-k89j for mapping verified Veteran temperature pages into the new core payload. Validation: cargo test -p cutout-core battery_page -- --nocapture; cargo test -p cutout-core; cargo test -p cutout-protocols veteran_bms -- --nocapture; cargo test -p cutout-protocols; cargo clippy -p cutout-core -p cutout-protocols --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic; cargo check -p cutout-cli; cargo fmt --all -- --check.

title: Replace ad hoc Veteran byte readers with bounded zero-copy parser helpers
description:
Replace scattered manual byte readers such as read_be_u32 with a small bounded zero-copy parser/field-reader layer for Veteran/NOSFET frames. Prefer standard/core APIs such as array slice conversion where enough; otherwise implement repr-transparent/newtype helpers for offsets, lengths, selectors, and big-endian reads so parser code states intent and keeps bounds checks centralized.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests cover successful and short-buffer reads, CRC field extraction, selector extraction, telemetry field offsets, and borrowed frame views without source-scanning tests. The helper must be zero-copy and zero-alloc in parser hot paths, no_std-friendly where practical, and should not expose raw buffer slicing decisions outside parser-owned modules. If an external crate is considered, document dependency cost and why std/core helpers are insufficient.
notes:
Parser design direction: use lots of semantic newtypes. For Veteran/NOSFET fixed-layout frames, prefer a tiny zero-copy/zero-alloc field-reader/frame-view layer built from core/standard APIs and zerocopy where it genuinely helps. Avoid nom/winnow-style parser-framework dependency for now: these frames are fixed binary layouts, so const offsets, borrowed frame views, typed selectors/lengths/CRC fields, and repr(transparent) units are likely clearer and cheaper than combinator grammar machinery. Revisit only if protocol grammar complexity grows enough to justify the dependency and abstraction cost.

Newtype requirements: add dedicated types for frame length, selector, CRC32 value, absolute offsets, payload/body views, BMS page selector, telemetry units, and channel identity where they prevent byte-index/units mistakes. Keep constructors const/inline where practical, expose getters instead of raw fields, and delete old ad hoc read_be_* helpers aggressively once tests cover the replacement. TDD first, no source-scanning tests, no hot-path allocation.
close_reason: Completed by parser-substrate slice: added a shared zero-copy ByteCursor with typed ByteOffset/ByteLen/ByteRange, migrated Veteran frame CRC/length reads plus Veteran telemetry and BMS page extraction off local read_be_* helpers, and validated parser short-read behavior, borrowed ranges, CRC/selector/telemetry paths, and Veteran swapped-u32 semantics. Remaining deeper semantic evidence newtypes for selector/page id, frame length, CRC value, body evidence, and ingest DTO boundaries are intentionally tracked by cutout-protocol-ingest-outcomes-ffy6.13; Begode reader migration is tracked by cutout-protocol-ingest-outcomes-ffy6.15.

title: Wire VESC stream decoder into read-only session
description: Use the bounded VescReadOnlyStreamDecoder from cutout-protocols inside a generic VESC ReadOnlySession model. Map Values replies into canonical TelemetryDelta with raw eRPM preserved, voltage/current/tachometer/fault/controller id carried without assuming a board speed profile, and map Stats replies into read-only diagnostics/statistics without actuator commands. Acceptance: TDD-first session tests prove link-up subscription/request behavior, chunked notification replay, canonical telemetry emission, unsupported actuator commands fail closed, public API exposes only libcutout-owned types, and cargo check -p cutout-cli remains green. No source-scanning tests.
notes: Implemented with one design adjustment: preserving raw eRPM directly in TelemetryDelta would require a compact raw-telemetry domain shape. A direct four-slot RawFieldValue attempt inflated SessionOutput from 128 to 224 bytes and was rejected. The landed slice preserves VESC raw eRPM/tachometer/controller/fault as bounded Diagnostics readbacks emitted alongside normalized voltage/current telemetry, while follow-up cutout-pwq9 tracks a compact first-class raw telemetry surface.
close_reason: Completed generic VESC read-only session wiring. Added common Nordic UART write/notify channel constants, VescRequestEncoder, VescGenericModel, and VescNotificationDecoder. The session subscribes on link-up, writes VESC GetValues for RequestTelemetry and GetStats for RequestDiagnostics, decodes chunked stream replies through VescReadOnlyStreamDecoder, maps voltage/current into TelemetryDelta without assuming speed from eRPM, preserves raw eRPM/tachometer/controller/fault and stats fields as bounded Diagnostics readbacks, and rejects actuation commands without writes. Validation: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test -p cutout-core, cargo test -p cutout-protocols, cargo clippy -p cutout-protocols --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic, cargo check -p cutout-cli, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo deny check with existing warning-only duplicate/unmatched-license notices.

title: Define capture and replay host API
description:
Define the core host-facing capture and replay API after HostSession exists. The flake/devshell work now gives us reproducible validation, and HostSession gives us a concrete sync facade. This issue should focus on a minimal, transport-independent capture stream for replaying HostSession inputs and comparing semantic outputs without BLE/runtime dependencies.

Scope: stable owned capture records for link up/down, notification bytes, ticks, and host commands; a replay helper that drives HostSession from those records; and tests proving whole-notification, one-byte, and arbitrary-chunk notification replay can produce equivalent semantic events for fake sessions.

Out of scope: advertisement/GATT inventory, user annotations, redaction metadata, on-disk PEVCAP/JSONL schema, BLE adapter collection, and concrete device captures.
design: Keep implementation in cutout-core as owned value types: CaptureRecord and CaptureReplaySummary or equivalent. Notification records own Vec<u8>; replay borrows only for the immediate HostSession call. Reuse HostSession::drain_outputs for semantic comparison. Provide small helper functions for replaying records and extracting events; avoid serde and file IO in this core slice. If capture metadata or file schema is needed, create child issues under capture/CLI rather than expanding this type layer.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for owned notification capture records, replay driving HostSession without BLE/runtime types, whole-notification versus one-byte replay equivalence, arbitrary-chunk replay equivalence, command/tick/link record replay, and output ordering preservation.
Capture/replay core types use stable explicit fields and owned payloads; no serde, file IO, async runtime, BLE, platform, or source-scanning tests are introduced.
Any larger advertisement/GATT inventory, annotation/redaction, on-disk schema, or capture CLI work discovered is added as beads issues.
Validation uses nix develop and includes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and cargo deny check. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.
notes: Implementation standard: follow Rust TDD red/green/refactor. Knowledge from HostSession: replay should drive the same facade methods hosts will use, and snapshots/diagnostics should be derived from emitted events rather than capture-specific hidden state. Keep this deterministic and low-allocation where practical.
close_reason: Completed: added core CaptureRecord and replay_capture API in cutout-core. Tests were added first and cover owned notification payloads, replay through HostSession without BLE/runtime types, link/tick/command/notification replay, output ordering, whole-notification versus one-byte replay equivalence, and arbitrary chunk replay equivalence. Added follow-ups cutout-5b5 for BLE inventory capture metadata and cutout-jpp for capture file schema plus CLI replay. Validated through nix develop: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and cargo deny check. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.

title: Reconnect session telemetry payloads to CLI output
description: The protocol session emits restored Veteran/Aero telemetry deltas, but the BTLE bridge only counted them and the CLI printed only counts. Reconnect telemetry payloads through SessionBridgeReport as an aggregated snapshot and render present normalized fields in connect/capture output. TDD acceptance: bridge tests prove telemetry snapshots aggregate deltas; CLI renderer tests prove present fields print and empty snapshots do not print.
close_reason: Session telemetry payloads now aggregate into SessionBridgeReport.telemetry_snapshot and the CLI prints present normalized telemetry fields after session summaries. Tests cover bridge snapshot aggregation and CLI rendering for populated and empty snapshots. Verification: nix develop -c cargo test -p cutout-btle -p cutout-cli -p cutout-protocols; nix develop -c cargo fmt --all -- --check; nix develop -c cargo clippy -p cutout-protocols -p cutout-btle -p cutout-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic; nix develop -c cargo check -p cutout-cli.

title: Complete NOSFET Aero read-only and dashboard integration
description:
Finish the NOSFET Aero path from live Bluetooth evidence through typed read-only protocol output and the CLI dashboard inspection surface. This epic collects the remaining Aero-specific work that is currently spread across capture, Veteran tail mapping, smart-BMS typing, dashboard integration, and later safe-control planning.

Scope: read-only Aero telemetry and BMS first; dashboard must display the same decoded model that CLI JSONL/capture replay sees; controls remain planned and disabled until explicit safety/control issues unblock them.

Standards: all implementation remains TDD-first, no source-scanning tests, bounded synchronous protocol logic, functional/low-allocation style where practical, and actual Bluetooth verification before declaring any newly typed Aero behavior fully specced.

Acceptance: Aero completion is visible as one tracked body of work: remaining labeled captures are recorded; Veteran tail semantics are mapped only with cross-state evidence; typed BMS temperatures/currents/status are exposed through core/protocol/session only after hardware verification; the dashboard shows live decoded Aero telemetry, firmware/settings readbacks, BMS pages, diagnostics, capture provenance, and reconnect/session state; controls are explicitly absent or disabled until safe-control dependencies close.
design:
Structure:
- Existing Aero protocol/capture/control issues keep their original parent-child homes and are linked here as related work, because Beads permits only one parent-child parent.
- New dashboard stories are direct children of this epic.
- Dashboard stories use blocks dependencies where implementation truly waits on protocol evidence, BMS mapping, capture provenance, control safety, or registry identification.

Implementation constraints:
- TDD-first for every code change.
- No source-scanning tests.
- Keep protocol decoding synchronous and transport-independent.
- Dashboard must consume the same session/read-only response model as CLI JSONL and PEVCAP replay.
- Raw/unverified Aero fields must stay visibly raw/unverified until hardware-gated mapping issues close.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
1. Remaining NF2557 capture labels are collected or explicitly deferred with rationale: rolling_forward, rolling_backward, lifted_wheel, charging, bms_screen, power_cycle.
2. Aero Veteran tail semantics have cross-state evidence before any new typed field is exposed.
3. BMS cell pages, verified temperature pages, verified metadata currents, raw/reserved pages, firmware/readbacks, diagnostics, and provenance are all represented in a dashboard-ready state model.
4. The live dashboard displays decoded Aero session data from actual SessionBridgeReport/read-only responses, not a separate parser.
5. PEVCAP replay can populate the same dashboard state for offline review.
6. Live NF2557 dashboard verification records Bluetooth/GATT/session evidence.
7. Controls remain absent/disabled until the safe-control and Aero command-capture blockers close.
notes:
Created as the organizing epic for the remaining Aero read-only/dashboard completion work. Existing protocol/capture issues remain under their original epics and are related here; new dashboard integration stories are children of this epic.

Implementation guidance:
- TDD-first. Aim for comprehensive behavioral coverage, including property tests where they add signal.
- Do not preserve legacy code for compatibility in this greenfield app; delete obsolete paths aggressively.
- Aggressive refactors are allowed when they improve the model. If a refactor is too large, create a new Beads issue describing the refactor before continuing.
- If an existing refactor issue no longer fits what we learned, update it or create a replacement issue instead of forcing the old shape.
- Avoid allocations in hot protocol/session/dashboard update paths unless avoiding them would make the implementation materially harder to maintain.
- Design for thousands of devices: maintainability, clear type boundaries, reusable data shapes, and evidence/provenance discipline are paramount.

Greenfield reminder: this is a greenfield app. Aggressively delete legacy code, compatibility shims, raw-event side channels, duplicated old paths, and obsolete APIs as soon as typed/tested coverage replaces them. Do not preserve old behavior for compatibility unless a current issue explicitly justifies it. If a deletion/refactor gets bigger than the issue in hand, create or update a Beads issue before continuing, then keep deleting instead of layering around the old design.

Standing implementation requirements: TDD-first; comprehensive behavioral coverage; property tests for parser/state-machine behavior where useful; mutation tests where they add signal; no source-scanning tests; low/no allocations in hot paths unless avoiding them makes the implementation materially less maintainable; design for thousands of devices, so maintainability and clear type boundaries are paramount.

title: Model dashboard-ready Aero read-only state
description:
Define the stable state shape that the dashboard consumes for Aero sessions. Today the dashboard mostly consumes TelemetrySnapshot and counters; the full Aero read-only stream also includes firmware, fixed-header settings/readbacks, BatteryPagePayload cell pages, raw BMS evidence, diagnostics, and provenance.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests define a dashboard-facing aggregate state built from SessionBridgeReport/DeviceEvent data without source scanning; it represents telemetry, firmware, settings, BMS page summaries, diagnostics, provenance, connection state, and unknown/unverified fields distinctly; it does not expose controls; bounded collections prevent unbounded dashboard growth; CLI JSONL and dashboard state derive from the same session data rather than separate interpretations.
notes:
Progress update: dashboard state now retains a bounded read-only summary from SessionBridgeReport::read_only_response_events instead of dropping those events after logging. The state tracks latest firmware summary, bounded settings summaries, bounded BMS page summaries, raw/metadata page count, diagnostic response count, and raw telemetry response count. This is intentionally dashboard-local for now so public core/API does not grow prematurely.

Learned follow-up for later dashboard slices: read-only formatting now has small local label helpers similar to CLI JSONL formatting. If rendering/JSONL/dashboard formatting diverges further, create a focused refactor issue to share display-label helpers without coupling the dashboard to JSON serialization.

Implementation guidance:
- TDD-first. Aim for comprehensive behavioral coverage, including property tests where they add signal.
- Do not preserve legacy code for compatibility in this greenfield app; delete obsolete paths aggressively.
- Aggressive refactors are allowed when they improve the model. If a refactor is too large, create a new Beads issue describing the refactor before continuing.
- If an existing refactor issue no longer fits what we learned, update it or create a replacement issue instead of forcing the old shape.
- Avoid allocations in hot protocol/session/dashboard update paths unless avoiding them would make the implementation materially harder to maintain.
- Design for thousands of devices: maintainability, clear type boundaries, reusable data shapes, and evidence/provenance discipline are paramount.
close_reason: Implemented dashboard-ready Aero read-only state slice. DashboardState now retains a bounded ReadOnlyDashboardState built from SessionBridgeReport::read_only_response_events: latest firmware summary, bounded settings summaries, bounded BMS page summaries, raw/metadata page counts, diagnostic response count, and raw telemetry response count. Tests cover read-only response aggregation and bounded BMS summary retention, alongside existing telemetry/provenance/session state tests. Rendering remains in cutout-95hn.3 and live hardware verification remains in cutout-95hn.5. Validation: nix develop -c cargo fmt --all -- --check; nix develop -c cargo test -p cutout-cli; nix develop -c cargo clippy -p cutout-cli --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic.

title: Correlate NOSFET app Left/Right battery pages to Veteran selector 3/7
description: Use timestamp-aligned NOSFET app Battery Info screenshots or screen recording plus live PEVCAP capture to determine whether app Left/Right temperature banks map to Veteran BMS selector 3 or 7. Do not infer physical side labels from value similarity alone, especially while charging because values drift. Acceptance: TDD-first fixture/correlation tests document the observed mapping, update dashboard/app-facing labels only after evidence is sufficient, preserve selector-number display until physical side mapping is verified, and record model, firmware, battery state, GATT inventory, app version, timestamps, capture labels, provenance, and redaction notes. notes: Dashboard under bacon follow-up after reading bacon source: bacon's MissionExecutor spawns the configured command as a direct child and its default kill path calls child.kill() on that process. title: Define PEVCAP capture format
description:
Define a versioned binary capture format, plus JSONL import/export for inspection. Records must include monotonic time, direction, characteristic UUID, write mode, and bytes; headers must include advertisements, services, write limits, platform identifier, resolved model/firmware, library version, registry hash, annotations, and wall-clock start.

Acceptance: the format can represent raw BLE sessions before a protocol is known and can be replayed deterministically later.
notes: Implementation update: cutout-core now has serde-feature PEVCAP JSONL import/export on the existing in-memory v1 model. The JSONL stream is deterministic: one header line with magic/version/header metadata followed by one ordered transport record per line. Tests cover header+record round-trip, model identity/annotations, role preservation, ordered records, and rejecting record-before-header input. Still missing before this format issue fully closes: compact binary container framing, CLI persistence, and mapping BridgeIdentityResolution into persisted PEVCAP headers from live BTLE sessions.
close_reason: Completed the PEVCAP v1 format definition in cutout-core. The in-memory envelope now carries version, header metadata, advertisements/services/GATT fingerprints, write limit, resolved identity fields, library version, registry hash, annotations, wall-clock start, and ordered transport records with monotonic time, direction, UUIDs, write mode, and bytes. Serde-feature JSONL import/export and binary container framing both round-trip the same model and reject malformed inputs. Remaining CLI persistence, BridgeIdentityResolution header population, raw capture, and replay tooling are tracked by cutout-capture-replay-validation-1kw.2, cutout-btleplug-cli-transport-27d.3, and replay follow-ups rather than this format-definition issue.

title: Define ProtocolSession reactor API
description:

title: Integrate polling plans into concrete NOSFET and Begode sessions
description:

Knowledge from the protocol crate: cutout-protocols is still a scaffold, while dedicated parser/capture issues already track real Veteran/NOSFET and Begode wire decoding. This slice should create deterministic session shells that prove polling-plan usage without pretending protocol byte encoders or parsers are complete.

Scope for this slice: add NOSFET Aero and Begode Falcon read-only session shells in cutout-protocols implementing ProtocolSession. On link/tick, each shell should enqueue a small polling plan, drain it in scheduler order, and emit transport write actions on family-specific placeholder GATT channels. Use core read-only commands and different plan order/urgency where useful. Keep implementation synchronous, transport-independent, bounded, and behavior-tested with fake host driving; no BLE, async runtimes, serde, or source-scanning tests.

Non-scope: actual Veteran DC 5A 5C frame bytes, Begode 55 AA bytes, notification parsers, GATT discovery, capture fixtures, identity registry, live hardware verification, and protocol-specific probe IDs. Add/link Beads follow-ups for any of those discovered gaps.

Device-specific parser/capture/hardware issues remain open for real protocol completion. Validation uses nix develop with focused tests, fmt, check, clippy, workspace tests, and cargo-deny. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.

title: Replace provisional probe encoder payloads with capture-backed bytes
description:
Replace provisional probe encoder payloads with real request bytes from captures/spec evidence, or explicitly encode no request when a family is passive. Current Aero/NOSFET evidence: live NF2557 read-only support subscribes to Veteran FFE1, receives DC 5A 5C telemetry/BMS long frames, resolves model id 43, and works with writes=0. Identity/model, firmware version, telemetry, and smart-BMS page metadata are passive fields in the notification stream. Therefore AeroRequestEncoder must not expose provisional aero:* write bytes for read-only probes.

Begode Falcon has source-backed ASCII N/V request bytes and separate hardware verification tracking; telemetry/BMS remains unsolicited there too.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests prove AeroRequestEncoder returns no encoded write for all current read-only probes/commands; Falcon N/V behavior remains intact; no source-scanning tests; protocol tests/clippy pass under nix develop. Any future Veteran control or settings writes must be implemented under safe-controls issues with capture proof, not by reusing read-only probes.

title: Capture NOSFET Aero read-only request bytes
description:
Acquire or check in source-attributed NOSFET/Veteran Aero read-only byte evidence for telemetry, identity/model, firmware, battery, and diagnostics probes. Source audit changed the implementation direction: NOSFET Aero should be treated as a Veteran/LeaperKim protocol-family wheel, and the wheel streams read-only telemetry unsolicited after notification subscription. Do not invent request bytes before parsing the notification stream.

Knowledge from live NF2557 smoke testing: macOS/CoreBluetooth exposes a platform UUID rather than a real MAC address; the device advertises service 0000ffe0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and discovers characteristic 0000ffe1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb with READ | WRITE_WITHOUT_RESPONSE | WRITE | NOTIFY. Earlier provisional sessions subscribed and wrote five placeholder requests; those writes are not protocol truth. Later live runs showed decoded telemetry events after subscription, confirming unsolicited streaming behavior.

Source audit: docs/protocol-source-audit.md records EUC Planet (MIT) as the clean-room-friendly source, WheelLog.Android (GPL-3.0) as corroborating evidence only, and EUC-Dash-ESP32 (GPL-3.0) as older background. EUC Planet documents NOSFET Aero as Veteran model id 43, 30 cells, 134 V Patton-family voltage range 9918..12337 raw centivolts, GATT ffe0/ffe1, dc5a5c Veteran magic, and 55aa Begode magic for same-GATT disambiguation.

Knowledge from the bounded payload work: TransportAction::Write now carries cutout_core::WritePayload with MAX_TRANSPORT_WRITE_LEN = 512, while current provisional protocol encoder payloads are ArrayVec-backed and capacity 24. The fixture schema must make oversized request evidence impossible to silently accept and should expose bytes as slices so tests and encoders can construct bounded payloads behaviorally.

Scope for this slice: add a small protocol request fixture model in cutout-protocols, without JSON/serde/file parsing yet. It should represent device family, probe, CommandKind, WriteMode, request bytes, optional service/characteristic GattChannel, provenance kind, and hardware verification status. It should validate command/probe family consistency and request-byte length against WritePayload.

No source-scanning tests. Validate through nix develop with focused tests, fmt, check, clippy, workspace tests, and cargo-deny.

title: Make transport write payloads bounded or borrowed
description:
The request encoder boundary can keep provisional bytes in ArrayVec, but ProtocolSession outputs currently use TransportAction::Write { bytes: Vec<u8> }, forcing a heap allocation/copy before the BTLE layer sees every write. This conflicts with the project preference for zero allocations where it does not take much longer and should be planned before high-rate polling or controls.

Acceptance: TDD-first design and implementation for write payload ownership. Either replace Vec with a bounded value type or add a borrowed/owned abstraction that keeps session output ergonomic without leaking lifetimes into frontends. Tests must exercise emitted writes behaviorally, not by source scanning. Validate through nix develop with fmt, check, clippy, workspace tests, and cargo-deny.
close_reason: Implemented with TDD: added failing WritePayload tests first, then introduced MAX_TRANSPORT_WRITE_LEN, WritePayload, and WritePayloadTooLong in cutout-core. TransportAction::Write now carries a bounded inline WritePayload instead of Vec<u8>, and protocol sessions convert encoded request bytes into bounded writes before emitting transport actions. Knowledge gained: a 512-byte inline payload avoids per-write heap allocation but makes TransportAction/SessionOutput large enough to need targeted clippy large_enum_variant allows; follow-up capacity measurement is tracked in cutout-core-reactor-domain-model-lkk.15.1 and intentionally remains open. Validated with nix develop: cargo test -p cutout-core write_payload, cargo test -p cutout-protocols session_emits, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo deny check.

title: Measure inline write payload capacity tradeoffs
description:
The bounded WritePayload implementation intentionally keeps up to 512 bytes inline to avoid per-write heap allocation, which makes TransportAction and SessionOutput large enough to require a targeted clippy::large_enum_variant allow. Before frontends and high-rate polling settle around this API, measure whether 512-byte inline capacity is the right default or whether the project should split small inline writes from rare large writes.

Acceptance: benchmark or size tests quantify SessionOutput/TransportAction size and common read-only write payload lengths; any capacity change is driven by behavior or measurements, not source scanning; TDD-first where code changes are made; validate through nix develop.
notes: Measurement update: exact size snapshots now show MAX_TRANSPORT_WRITE_LEN=512, WritePayload=516 bytes, TransportAction=536 bytes, SessionOutput=536 bytes, RequestQueue<3>=104 bytes, RequestScheduler<3>=184 bytes, RequestQueue<8>=264 bytes, RequestScheduler<8>=344 bytes, and RequestSchedulerDiagnostics=72 bytes. Protocol request measurements show the only current write-backed Falcon read-only requests, N and V, are each 1 byte; Aero/Veteran read probes are passive. This argues for a follow-up split between small common-case write payloads and rare large writes rather than changing capacity blindly in this measurement slice.
close_reason: Measured inline write and scheduler size tradeoffs with tests: WritePayload 516 bytes, TransportAction/SessionOutput 536 bytes, RequestQueue<3> 104 bytes, RequestScheduler<3> 184 bytes, RequestQueue<8> 264 bytes, RequestScheduler<8> 344 bytes, diagnostics 72 bytes, queued request 32 bytes. Added protocol test showing current source-backed Falcon N/V writes are 1 byte while Veteran/Aero read probes are passive. Created cutout-jey6 to split small common-case writes from rare large writes instead of changing capacity blindly. title: Define canonical telemetry delta and snapshot model
description:
Define the canonical telemetry model in cutout-core now that the synchronous reactor API exists. Telemetry should be represented as partial deltas with fixed integer units, source and quality metadata, and an aggregator that updates a snapshot without treating absent fields as zero.

Acceptance: unknown remains distinct from zero; battery/input current is distinct from motor/phase current; controller, motor, and battery temperatures are separate; reported speed, calculated speed, reported battery percent, and app-estimated battery percent can coexist; telemetry can be emitted through DeviceEvent without introducing async, BLE, UUID, floating-point, or platform types.
design: Keep this issue to the core value model: Measured<T>, ValueSource, ValueQuality, TelemetryDelta, TelemetrySnapshot, apply_delta, and a DeviceEvent::Telemetry variant. Use fixed units in field names such as speed_mm_s, voltage_mv, current_ma, power_mw, temperature_mc, pwm_permille, distance_mm, pitch_mdeg, and roll_mdeg. Do not add protocol-specific raw diagnostics here; diagnostics counters and raw field events belong to the parser diagnostics issue.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for partial deltas updating snapshots, absent fields preserving prior values, zero values remaining real measurements, and distinct current/temperature/battery estimate fields.
Telemetry public types derive Debug/Clone/Copy/Eq/PartialEq where practical and compile under Rust 2024 with the workspace lint policy.
DeviceEvent can carry a TelemetryDelta without pulling protocol, runtime, BLE, UUID, or mobile dependencies into cutout-core.
Validation includes cargo check, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace.
notes: Implementation standard: start from a failing test and keep the work TDD-first. Use property tests where they add signal, but this issue can stay with focused unit tests unless a stateful aggregator invariant needs broader coverage. Prefer fixed integer units and low-allocation structs. Setup findings still apply: cargo-deny is not installed locally, and miri is unavailable for the pinned stable 1.96.0 aarch64-apple-darwin toolchain.
close_reason: Completed: fixed-unit TelemetryDelta, TelemetrySnapshot, Measured metadata, and DeviceEvent::Telemetry added with tests for partial updates, known zero, and distinct current/temperature/percent fields; validated cargo check, fmt, clippy, and test

Acceptance: hosts can inspect command kind, safety class, and support/refusal status before any protocol session emits a TransportAction; unsupported commands have structured reasons; command metadata stays in cutout-core without pulling in protocol, BLE, runtime, UUID, or mobile dependencies.

Do not implement protocol-specific write bytes, scheduler behavior, arming tokens, or stationary validation here; those belong to later safety/control and scheduler issues. Avoid raw command bytes in public API.

title: Implement parser limits, errors, and diagnostics counters
description: Define shared parser limits, parser errors, and diagnostics counters in cutout-core now that SessionInput, DeviceEvent, telemetry, commands, and capabilities exist. This issue should provide bounded, transport-independent vocabulary for protocol parsers: frame length limits, queue/event limits, timeout thresholds, malformed-input errors, and saturating counters for dropped bytes, resynchronizations, bad checksums, timeouts, oversized frames, and unmatched replies.\n\nAcceptance: malformed wire input can be represented as typed errors without panics; diagnostic counters can be incremented and emitted through DeviceEvent for inspector/CLI use; no protocol-specific parser logic, BLE/runtime types, UUID types, or allocations are introduced beyond existing Vec-backed transport actions.

Use fixed integer counts and saturating increments so telemetry sessions can continue after noisy wire input. Do not implement Veteran/Begode parsers here; protocol-specific parser property tests remain in protocol driver issues. A separate follow-up issue tracks host-facing diagnostic serialization for CLI/FFI so this issue stays focused on core types.

title: Implement polling, retry, pacing, and command correlation primitives
description:
Define reusable, transport-independent scheduling primitives in cutout-core now that commands, capabilities, parser limits, and parser diagnostics exist. This issue should cover the common state needed by protocol sessions to pace writes, serialize ambiguous requests, enforce deadlines, count retries, and classify replies without depending on BLE runtimes or protocol-specific packet bytes.

Scope: request keys, in-flight request state, retry/pacing limits, timeout decisions, and correlation outcomes that can increment ParserDiagnostics::timeouts or ::unmatched_replies. This should be enough for NOSFET/Begode read-only sessions and later Refloat package broadcasts to avoid overlapping requests where replies cannot be disambiguated.

Out of scope: concrete telemetry polling policy, protocol-specific command bytes, async timers, BLE queues, FFI DTOs, and Refloat package implementation.
design: Keep the implementation in cutout-core as Copy/Eq-friendly value types with no heap allocation: RequestKey, RequestPolicy, ScheduledRequest, CorrelationResult, and a small RequestTracker for one in-flight request per ambiguous key/class. Prefer const constructors and pure transition methods over callbacks. The tracker should operate on host-supplied MonotonicMillis and return typed decisions instead of sleeping or spawning timers. If multi-slot queueing becomes necessary, create a child issue rather than inflating this slice.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for write pacing, timeout/retry eligibility, successful reply correlation clearing the in-flight slot, unmatched replies incrementing diagnostics, and serialization of ambiguous overlapping requests.
Core scheduler types do not introduce Vec/String/async/BLE/runtime/mobile dependencies.
Timeout and unmatched-reply paths can be reflected through existing ParserDiagnostics counters.
Validation includes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace; cargo-deny/miri blockers remain tracked by cutout-gj1 unless the environment changes.
notes: Implementation standard: start from failing tests and keep this TDD-first. The parser diagnostics work showed that timeout/unmatched-reply accounting belongs in shared core, but protocol-specific property tests should stay with concrete parser/session issues. Keep this slice deterministic, synchronous, bounded, and low-allocation. Actual Bluetooth verification is required when a device/protocol is fully specced, not for these core primitives.
close_reason: Completed: added RequestKey, RequestPolicy, ScheduledRequest, RequestTracker, RequestStartError, RequestTick, and CorrelationResult as synchronous one-slot scheduler primitives. Tests were added first and cover write pacing, timeout/retry eligibility, successful reply correlation clearing the slot, unmatched replies incrementing ParserDiagnostics, and serialization of ambiguous overlaps. title: Design concrete host API for CLI, Swift, and Kotlin
description:
Design and prove the concrete host-facing session API shape now that core has ProtocolSession, telemetry, command metadata, parser diagnostics, and request scheduling primitives. The API must be usable by CLI and future UniFFI hosts without exposing generic Rust traits, borrowed buffers, async streams, BLE/CoreBluetooth/Android types, or protocol-specific packet internals.

Scope for this issue: define the minimal core facade vocabulary and behavior around owned notification input, link events, commands, ticks, drainable outputs, current snapshot access, and diagnostics access. This should be test-proven in cutout-core with a fake ProtocolSession so later CLI, Swift, and Kotlin work can bind to concrete value types instead of designing the lifecycle repeatedly.

Out of scope: UniFFI generation, Swift/Kotlin project files, BLE adapters, JSON serialization, capture file formats, and protocol-specific sessions.
design: Introduce a small HostSession wrapper or equivalent concrete facade in cutout-core that owns a protocol session and an output buffer. Prefer sync methods: ingest_link_up, ingest_link_down, ingest_notification_owned, tick, issue_command, drain_outputs, current_snapshot, diagnostics. Avoid borrowed buffers in stored state; borrowed notification input is allowed only inside the immediate call into ProtocolSession. Keep the facade generic internally if needed for Rust tests, but do not let the future FFI surface depend on generic traits. If stable DTO/serialization naming grows larger, keep it in cutout-core-reactor-domain-model-lkk.6.1.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for driving a fake session through host-facing methods, owned notification ingestion without retaining borrowed buffers, draining outputs without exposing the internal Vec, snapshot updates from telemetry events, diagnostics updates from diagnostic events, and command issuance through the same facade.
The accepted API avoids platform transport types, async runtimes, generic trait objects across intended host boundaries, and borrowed output streams.
Any larger lifecycle, capture, DTO, or queueing work discovered is added as beads issues rather than skipped.
Validation includes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace; cargo-deny/miri blockers remain tracked by cutout-gj1 unless the environment changes.
notes: Implementation standard: follow Rust TDD red/green/refactor. The scheduler primitive work showed the host layer needs to own buffering and expose drain operations, while protocol sessions stay synchronous and transport-independent. Keep this slice deterministic and low-allocation where practical; actual Bluetooth verification belongs to concrete device completion issues.
close_reason: Completed: added HostSession<S> facade in cutout-core with sync host methods for link up/down, owned notification ingestion, ticks, commands, drain_outputs, current_snapshot, and diagnostics. Added follow-ups cutout-8fm for capture/replay API and cutout-z6t for concrete UniFFI object boundary; child cutout-core-reactor-domain-model-lkk.6.1 remains open for diagnostic serialization. title: Define host-facing diagnostic serialization shape

Define stable host-facing diagnostic DTOs in cutout-core now that ParserDiagnostics, ParserError, DeviceEvent::Diagnostics, and HostSession::diagnostics exist. Provide conversion helpers from ParserDiagnostics, ParserError, and diagnostic DeviceEvent.

Out of scope: serde/JSON formatting, UniFFI generation, Swift/Kotlin project code, capture file schema, and localized/display strings.
design: Keep this in cutout-core as Copy/Eq-friendly value types: DiagnosticSnapshot, DiagnosticErrorKind, DiagnosticError, and helper constructors/from_* functions. Use fixed integer units and Option fields instead of borrowed strings. Do not add serde yet; actual wire/JSON naming should be implemented in CLI/capture issues using this DTO surface. HostSession already accumulates ParserDiagnostics, so expose a stable conversion from HostSession::diagnostics() rather than adding host-specific serialization state.
acceptance_criteria:
Failing tests are added first for ParserDiagnostics-to-DiagnosticSnapshot field mapping, ParserError-to-DiagnosticError mapping for oversized frame and timeout details, DeviceEvent::Diagnostics-to-DiagnosticSnapshot mapping, and HostSession diagnostics conversion.
DTOs use stable explicit fields, no borrowed buffers, no serde/runtime/mobile dependencies, and Copy/Eq where practical.
Any larger JSONL, capture schema, or UniFFI binding work discovered is added as beads issues rather than skipped.

close_reason: Completed: added DiagnosticSnapshot, DiagnosticErrorKind, and DiagnosticError as stable host-facing diagnostic DTOs in cutout-core. title: Expand read-only command vocabulary for device probes
description:
Expand the transport-independent read-only command vocabulary now that PollRequest/PollingPlan can only schedule existing CommandKind values. Knowledge from cutout-jud: polling plans correctly reject non-read-only commands, but identity and telemetry are too narrow for NOSFET/Begode/VESC read-only sessions. title: Add project flake/devshell for reproducible validation
description: Add a repo-owned full Nix flake so contributors can build, run, and validate the project without relying on host-global cargo tools or the absent fallback ~/cfg/devshells path. design: Use a repo-owned flake with nixpkgs plus a Rust overlay capable of reading rust-toolchain.toml for the stable toolchain. Include cargo-deny from nixpkgs and expose a nightly cargo/miri command path for cargo miri test without relying on the pinned stable toolchain. Validate behavior with nix develop -c commands rather than source-scanning tests. If nightly Miri cannot be made available cleanly on Darwin from the selected inputs, add a follow-up issue documenting the blocker instead of hiding it.
acceptance_criteria:
nix develop works from the repo root.
The flake exposes packages, apps, formatter, and checks, not only a devShell.
Inside nix develop, cargo, rustc, cargo fmt, clippy, cargo-deny, and nixfmt are available from the shell.

title: Refactor Aero protocol implementation for maintainability and allocation discipline
description:
Refactor the Aero/Veteran protocol implementation created during the first hardware-supported slice so it is easier to extend to Begode Falcon, VESC/Refloat, iOS/Android FFI, and future Veteran/NOSFET work.

Goals: clearer module boundaries, smaller pure functions, functional-style decoding pipelines where practical, bounded buffers instead of incidental heap allocation, explicit provenance/verification types, and comprehensive behavioral tests. This epic must not change read-only behavior without failing tests first.

Standards: TDD-first, no source-scanning tests, Rust 2024, clippy pedantic, fmt, cargo-deny where relevant, property tests for parser/session invariants, mutation tests where they add signal, miri still skipped unless the project decision changes. Keep protocol logic synchronous and transport-independent; async runtimes remain adapter-only.
notes: Refactor complete for current source: legacy read-only session aliases are gone; the active API is ReadOnlySession<Model, const ACCEPT_ANY_NOTIFICATION: bool> over ZST model specs; typed operation capability traits/session gates are complete; Veteran BMS selector/count handling is split into a bounded protocol module with property tests; focused cargo-mutants targets for current request/session/BMS surfaces have no missed mutants. The historical VeteranFrameReassembler mutation target was moved to a new Aero follow-up because that parser surface is absent in the current tree. Do not reintroduce model-specific session wrappers or source-scanning tests.
close_reason: Completed the refactor epic against the current source tree. All direct children are closed. Current protocol code uses ZST model specs, const-generic read-only sessions, typed operation capability traits, bounded Veteran BMS selector/count decoding, focused behavioral/property tests, and targeted cargo-mutants runs with no missed mutants on current surfaces. Missing future Veteran frame parser restoration is tracked outside this refactor epic rather than hidden inside it.

title: Design typed read/write/control capability traits
description:
Design and implement the next protocol trait layer after the generic read-only session refactor. Current code now has ZST model specs (NosfetAeroModel, BegodeFalconModel), Manufacturer, ReadOnlyModelSpec, and ReadOnlySession<Model, const ACCEPT_ANY_NOTIFICATION: bool>. The remaining design gap is that read/write/control capability is still represented mostly as Capabilities plus an ad hoc DeviceCommand ignore match inside the session handler.

Move toward separate static traits/newtypes for read-only request capability, benign write/settings capability, and dangerous actuation capability so models expose supported operations through type bounds instead of dynamic command filtering. Prefer ZST specs, associated consts, const generics for bounded behavior, small enums/newtypes for safety classes, and pure transition helpers. Keep automatic identification/probing read-only and ensure write/control traits cannot be accidentally invoked by read-only sessions.

Acceptance: protocol family, manufacturer, model, transport channels, read capabilities, write capabilities, and safety class are explicit in types; unsupported write/control paths fail closed by construction or by tested diagnostics; compile/runtime tests prove read-only sessions cannot schedule writes or dangerous actuation; no legacy AeroReadOnlySession/FalconReadOnlySession aliases or monolithic wrapper return.
notes: Current evidence: c9608a1 removed legacy read-only session aliases and introduced ReadOnlySession<Model, const ACCEPT_ANY_NOTIFICATION: bool> over ZST model specs. Commit 572429a added ProtocolModelSpec, ProtocolOperation marker ZSTs, and read/write/control/actuation capability traits. The read-only session command path now uses a SupportsReadRequests capability gate instead of a broad DeviceCommand ignore match. Remaining child work is cutout-hnp.14.3: model safe settings writes separately from actuation before any control surface is enabled.
close_reason: Typed operation capability design is complete for the refactor epic: ProtocolModelSpec and operation marker ZSTs are public, read/write/control/actuation capability traits exist, read-only sessions use SupportsReadRequests capability gates, unsupported write/control/actuation commands fail closed with no transport action, and control-specific implementation work has been moved to the safe-controls epic.

title: Define Veteran BMS page selector and cell-count invariants
description:

Current code already has generic BatteryPageKind, BatteryPageMetadata, BatteryCellVoltagePage, BatteryRawPage, and BatteryPagePayload in cutout-core, but there is not yet a proven Veteran/NOSFET selector map or cell-count invariant layer. Acceptance: live or fixture-backed evidence identifies selector mapping and per-page cell-count invariants; each page class records verification status; if evidence is incomplete, unknown pages remain raw/unsupported rather than normalized; newly discovered parser/decoder work is split into children instead of guessing.
notes: Evidence used: live hardware NOSFET Aero NF2557 fixture crates/cutout-protocols/fixtures/nosfet-aero/nf2557-2026-06-21-bms-pages.hex. The capture annotation records macOS CoreBluetooth, FFE0/FFE1 GATT, writes=0, subscribes=1, notifications=93, telemetry=19, and live hardware provenance. Observed rotating selectors include 00..08. The implemented conservative model types 01/02/05/06 as 16-value cell-voltage pages, 00/04 as metadata pages, and leaves 03/07/08 plus all unknown selectors raw. Individual cell voltages are not yet represented in core; this slice validates selector/count typing and preserves raw fallback instead of normalizing unverified pages.
close_reason: Defined the conservative Veteran/NOSFET BMS selector model from live Aero fixture evidence: 01/02/05/06 are 16-value cell pages, 00/04 are metadata, 03/07/08 and unknown selectors remain raw. title: Implement protocol polling plans using scheduler primitives
description:
Implement transport-independent protocol polling plan primitives now that RequestQueue and RequestUrgency exist. Knowledge from cutout-4b3/cutout-vee: core can queue bounded RequestKey/RequestPolicy pairs, prioritize by urgency, and preserve FIFO within urgency, but current CommandKind only has read-only identity and telemetry. Do not smuggle NOSFET/Begode BMS or diagnostics probes into this slice before the command vocabulary exists.

Scope for this slice: add a small Copy/Eq polling plan type in cutout-core that maps a fixed list of read-only poll items into QueuedRequest values with explicit urgency and policy, and can enqueue those items into a RequestQueue using enqueue_by_urgency. The plan should reject non-read-only command kinds, surface duplicate/capacity failures through structured errors, and remain sync/transport-independent/no allocation.

Non-scope: protocol-specific poll cadence, device-specific BMS/diagnostic command kinds, BLE action generation, retry execution, starvation aging, scheduler diagnostics counters, or real NOSFET/Begode parser sessions. Add/link Beads follow-ups for those rather than skipping them.

Acceptance: failing tests first for plan items converting to queued requests, non-read-only rejection, priority enqueue order, duplicate propagation, capacity propagation, and property-tested read-only acceptance. Tests must use behavior assertions, not source scanning. Validation uses nix develop with focused tests, fmt, check, clippy, workspace tests, and cargo-deny. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.
close_reason: Implemented core polling-plan primitives without protocol-specific command expansion. Added PollRequest, PollingPlan, and PollingPlanError in cutout-core; plans convert only read-only commands into QueuedRequest values and enqueue through enqueue_by_urgency, propagating duplicate and capacity queue errors. title: Modularize cutout-btle transport adapter
description:
Split the current 4k-line cutout-btle/src/lib.rs into small, behavior-preserving modules with clear ownership. This is a greenfield app, so the goal is not compatibility with the current file layout; the goal is a maintainable transport adapter crate whose public API is obvious and whose internals have narrow seams.

Current lib.rs owns too much: scan/observation formatting, connection discovery, GATT summaries, session bridge driving, notification window processing, capture/PEVCAP conversion, reconnect orchestration, identity hints, output/report processing, btleplug adapter glue, errors, helpers, and hundreds of tests. Refactor it into modules that each have one reason to change while preserving the public crate surface through re-exports during the migration.
design:
Target module shape:
- lib.rs: public crate docs, public re-exports, minimal module declarations only.
- observation.rs: PeripheralObservation, manufacturer data summaries, advertised service/name family hints, observation display helpers.
- target.rs: ConnectionTarget matching and address normalization.
- gatt.rs: CharacteristicSummary, ServiceSummary, ConnectionSummary, SessionEndpoints, GATT role helpers, write/notify candidate selection.
- error.rs: BtleError, SessionBridgeError, backend_call, diagnostic hints.
- peripheral.rs: SessionPeripheral trait, btleplug Peripheral impl, ConnectedPeripheral if still useful.
- scan.rs: first_adapter, scan_peripherals, collect_observations, find_peripheral, wait_for_scan_match, observation_from_peripheral.
- bridge.rs: drive_session entry points, DriveSessionConfig, process_link_up_outputs, process_notification_window, process_session_outputs, notification decode outcome handling.
- capture.rs: SessionCaptureRecord, SessionCapture, raw notification capture, capture-to-PEVCAP conversion, capture metadata.
- reconnect.rs: ReconnectingSessionHost, BtleplugReconnectHost, reconnect capture reports and orchestration.
- identity.rs: BridgeIdentityResolution, IdentityContext/State, identity report updates.
- report.rs: SessionBridgeReport, SessionBridgeEvent, merge/report update helpers.
- hex/display helpers should move next to their owning type or be deleted if only tests need them.

Rules:
- Start TDD-first for every extraction with behavior/compile tests where the seam is risky.
- No source-scanning tests.
- Preserve async runtime/BLE stack only in cutout-btle; protocol semantics stay in core/protocols.
- Prefer private modules plus explicit public re-exports. Do not make everything pub just to appease tests.
- Keep raw BTLE notification bytes treated as untrusted input. Capture/provenance may store raw bytes; bridge/session/report code should carry typed protocol outcomes once parser-owned results exist.
- Delete compatibility shims aggressively once the public surface is re-exported cleanly.
- If any extraction exposes a deeper API design problem, create/update a child issue rather than hiding it with a facade.
acceptance_criteria:
1. cutout-btle/src/lib.rs is reduced to module declarations, crate docs, and intentional public re-exports.
2. Public API remains source-compatible for current cutout-cli/cutout-mobile/cutout-protocol callers unless a child issue explicitly deletes a weak API.
3. Session bridge, capture, reconnect, scan/discovery, GATT summary, identity, report, and backend adapter code each live in focused modules.
4. Tests are moved near the modules they exercise or into integration-style tests where that keeps private APIs private.
5. Workspace validation remains green after each extraction: cargo fmt, cargo nextest for affected packages, cargo check -p cutout-cli, and clippy pedantic for affected crates.
6. No module keeps raw notification interpretation above the parser boundary; parser-owned typed results from cutout-protocol-ingest-outcomes-ffy6.16 are accommodated cleanly.
7. The final module graph has no circular conceptual dependencies: scan/connect produce summaries, bridge drives sessions, capture records evidence, report summarizes typed outputs, and protocol semantics remain outside cutout-btle.
close_reason: Completed cutout-btle modularization: lib.rs is crate docs/module declarations/grouped re-exports, scan/target/GATT/error/peripheral/bridge/report/capture/reconnect/identity/battery code live in focused modules, BTLE scan no longer owns family/model hints, and raw notification handling stays at explicit parser/capture boundaries. Validated fmt check, workspace nextest, workspace pedantic clippy, cargo deny check, and cargo check -p cutout-cli.

title: Refactor notification ingest into typed protocol outcomes
description:
Refactor notification ingest so BTLE protocol bytes are treated as untrusted input and validated at the first protocol boundary. The intended flow is: BLE bytes arrive -> explicit capture/provenance may record raw bytes -> selected protocol parser/framer immediately returns typed parser operations/results, typed evidence, and typed domain events -> raw payload bytes become inaccessible to normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile code.

This epic is not about making raw logs prettier. It is about making invalid states and raw-leak paths difficult or impossible: no uuid/service/len strings as protocol meaning, no primitive selector/tag/body_len/event_count bags above parser/core, no output-Vec side-effect inference, and no presentation-layer reconstruction of semantics from raw buffers.
design:
Threat model:
- Treat BTLE notifications as untrusted user input.
- Parser/framer internals and explicit capture/provenance artifacts are the only places raw bytes may live.
- The parser boundary validates structure and returns typed complete/incomplete/error/reserved/gap outcomes.
- Higher layers consume typed operations/results, typed telemetry/read-only/domain events, and typed evidence only.

Type strategy:
- Move from bags to types as early as possible.
- Use repr-transparent newtypes with ZST/PhantomData markers for frame length, payload/body length, selector/page id, tag/opcode, semantic event count, units, verification state, provenance, and parser state.
- Use sealed traits/marker traits/const generics for manufacturer/family/model capability, channel role, read-only/control surfaces, and fixed-size protocol structures where they make invalid combinations unrepresentable.
- Keep protocol engine synchronous, bounded, transport-independent, and low/no-allocation in hot paths.

Architecture:
- Parser-owned operation/result types should mirror the nntp-proxy style: parse/classify once, preserve borrowed spans or bounded tiny evidence inside parser-owned types, and expose only validated semantics upward.
- BTLE bridge carries typed outcomes; it may count/capture raw notifications but never assigns semantics from raw bytes, UUID/service strings, or report event counts.
- Dashboard/log/CLI/FFI/mobile code are edge consumers. They may format typed values but must not recover protocol meaning from raw transport data.
- Raw Debug/display/logging is a potential side channel. Known protocol traffic should not be printable as raw payload except through explicit capture/provenance/debug artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Raw BLE notification bytes are only available to explicit capture/provenance artifacts and protocol parser internals; normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile APIs cannot access raw payload bytes for known protocol traffic.
2. The first protocol boundary emits typed parser operations/results and typed evidence using core/protocol newtypes for selector/page id, tag/opcode, notification length, payload/body length, semantic event count, channel roles where practical, units, and provenance/verification.
3. Known protocol notifications cannot surface to dashboard/session report/mobile as generic uuid/service/len raw events, primitive evidence bags, or late-formatted strings.
4. Buffered fragments, complete semantic frames, parser diagnostics, known-reserved payloads, parser gaps, and ignored/wrong-channel traffic are distinct typed outcomes.
5. BTLE bridge, PEVCAP replay, dashboard/logging, and FFI/mobile all consume the same typed outcome semantics without transport-specific reinterpretation.
6. Hot ingest paths are allocation-free or explicitly justified with tests/benchmarks; core/session/output types remain bounded.
7. Regression/property tests cover fragmentation, coalescing, malformed frames, known-reserved frames, parser gaps, ignored channels, no-raw-leak invariants, and primitive/unit mix-up prevention.
8. Existing Aero live dashboard behavior is reverified against actual Bluetooth hardware after parser-first typed migration.
notes:
Correction from implementation review: this epic is about early typing, not late string rendering. Do not paper over primitive/raw protocol shapes with CLI/dashboard formatting wrappers. If data reaches presentation as raw bytes, uuid/service/len strings, selector/tag/body_len primitive bags, or ad hoc display text, the parser boundary failed.

Greenfield reminder: aggressively delete legacy raw-event plumbing and compatibility shapes. If a refactor gets larger than a child issue, create/update child issues, then keep moving the type boundary earlier rather than layering around weak old shapes.

Standing implementation requirements: TDD-first; comprehensive behavioral coverage; property tests for parser/state-machine behavior where useful; mutation tests where they add signal; no source-scanning tests; low/no allocations in notification hot paths unless avoiding them makes the code meaningfully less maintainable; design for thousands of devices and keep maintenance/type boundaries paramount.

Design preference: prefer small repr-transparent newtypes, ZST markers, const generics, and sealed/marker traits for parser state, protocol family, model capability, channel roles, selectors, tags, lengths, counters, and unit-bearing values. Use them where they remove invalid states or unit confusion, not as decorative wrapper taxonomy.

Threat model update 2026-06-23: treat BTLE protocol bytes like untrusted user input. Raw bytes enter transport/capture and parser internals only; after the first protocol boundary, normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile code should only see typed parser results, typed evidence, and typed domain events. If raw bytes, uuid/service/len strings, primitive selector/tag/body_len/event_count bags, or late format-string reconstruction reach ordinary application code, the parser boundary failed.
