Prefer repr-transparent newtypes with ZST/PhantomData markers, sealed traits, const generics, and parser-owned operation/result enums where they make invalid states unrepresentable: channel roles, family/model capability, parser state, frame length, payload length, selector/page id, tag/opcode, counters, telemetry units, verification/provenance, and presentation state. Raw access is allowed only through explicit capture/provenance/debug artifacts with bounded metadata.

Implementation rule: start TDD-first, add property tests for parser/framer/state-machine behavior, use mutation tests where they add signal, keep hot ingest paths zero-allocation unless the alternative harms maintainability, and delete legacy raw/primitive/stringly compatibility paths aggressively. title: Reverify Aero dashboard over Bluetooth after ingest refactor
description: Run the migrated parser-first typed-ingest pipeline against the live NF2557 Aero after the core/protocol/BTLE/dashboard changes land. This is the hardware gate proving known protocol traffic is parsed immediately into typed outcomes/evidence, raw bytes do not leak above capture/provenance, buffered fragments/reserved pages/parser gaps are distinct typed evidence, and parsed telemetry/read-only outputs still appear correctly.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Live NF2557 Aero verification runs after parser-first typed evidence and parser-owned operation/result changes are in place.
2. Record model, firmware, battery/profile, app/library version, GATT inventory, labels, charging/idle/load state, provenance, redaction notes, and actual Bluetooth verification evidence.
3. Dashboard/session events show typed semantic telemetry, BMS/read-only responses, buffered progress, selector 8 reserved evidence, parser gaps, diagnostics, and ignored traffic without raw uuid/service/len fallback for known traffic.
4. Raw bytes appear only in explicit capture/provenance/debug artifacts, not normal dashboard/report/mobile state.
5. Any still-raw or unverified event becomes a parser gap issue with bounded typed evidence, not a skipped observation.
notes:
Update after epic correction: live verification must check the actual data-flow invariant, not just that logs look nicer. Capture/log evidence should show: raw bytes are only in explicit capture/debug.log capture paths; normal dashboard/session events are typed semantic/fragment/reserved/gap/diagnostic outcomes; selector 8 appears as typed reserved evidence; any parser gaps carry typed bounded evidence; no uuid/service/len raw-notification fallback is used for known protocol traffic. Charging/idle/load state remains required metadata.

Standing constraints: TDD-first before hardware runs, using capture-backed fixtures and property tests where useful; no source-scanning tests; aggressively delete stale live/dashboard/raw-event behavior once typed coverage replaces it; if live evidence exposes a larger refactor, create/update issues instead of skipping it; keep hot-path allocations bounded/justified; record model, firmware, battery/profile, app/library version, GATT inventory, labels, provenance, redaction notes, and actual Bluetooth verification before closing.

Threat model update 2026-06-23: treat BTLE protocol bytes like untrusted user input. Raw bytes enter transport/capture and parser internals only; after the first protocol boundary, normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile code should only see typed parser results, typed evidence, and typed domain events. If raw bytes, uuid/service/len strings, primitive selector/tag/body_len/event_count bags, or late format-string reconstruction reach ordinary application code, the parser boundary failed.

Design implication: move from bags to types. Prefer repr-transparent newtypes with ZST/PhantomData markers, sealed traits, const generics, and parser-owned operation/result enums where they make invalid states unrepresentable: channel roles, family/model capability, parser state, frame length, payload length, selector/page id, tag/opcode, counters, telemetry units, verification/provenance, and presentation state. Raw access is allowed only through explicit capture/provenance/debug artifacts with bounded metadata.

Implementation rule: start TDD-first, add property tests for parser/framer/state-machine behavior, use mutation tests where they add signal, keep hot ingest paths zero-allocation unless the alternative harms maintainability, and delete legacy raw/primitive/stringly compatibility paths aggressively. If the typed boundary work gets bigger than the issue in hand, create/update child issues rather than layering around weak shapes.

title: Clean up downstream CLI/dashboard string rendering after parser-first typing
description:
Downstream presentation still has Vec<String> field bags, repeated push_measured_* helpers, format!/join chains, and hand-rendered telemetry/firmware/settings strings. This is a symptom and cleanup target after parser-first typed evidence is corrected; it is not the core architecture fix and should not distract from moving types earlier.

When addressed, delete bespoke string-rendering patterns in favor of typed presentation state or structured tracing/output at the edge. Do not add wrapper taxonomy or layers for their own sake.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CLI/dashboard presentation consumes typed domain/evidence/presentation state and does not receive raw payloads or primitive parser bags.
2. Remove Vec<String>/format!/join helper patterns from hot/internal paths; final formatting happens only at IO/render edges.
3. Use presentation newtypes/structured render state for units, chart bounds, battery/profile values, and event summaries where it prevents unit or state confusion.
4. Tests assert structured render state and representative output behavior without source scanning.
5. If presentation cleanup reveals parser/core raw leaks, update the parser issue instead of hiding it with late wrappers.
notes:
Update after epic correction: do not work this before .14 and .13 unless directly necessary. The actual ingest architecture is data-in -> parser-first typed evidence -> raw inaccessible except capture/provenance. This issue only cleans downstream presentation once typed evidence/domain state already exists. Do not add wrapper taxonomy or late string renderers as a substitute for earlier typing.

Standing constraints: TDD-first; no source-scanning tests; aggressively delete legacy Vec<String>/format!/join/raw-render paths once typed presentation state exists; if presentation cleanup reveals a deeper parser/core issue, create/update that issue instead of hiding it here; avoid allocations except final IO/artifact boundaries; assert typed presentation/structured output rather than implementation-shaped string assembly; keep dashboard/CLI render state maintainable for thousands of device models.

Raw bytes enter transport/capture and parser internals only; after the first protocol boundary, normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile code should only see typed parser results, typed evidence, and typed domain events. If raw bytes, uuid/service/len strings, primitive selector/tag/body_len/event_count bags, or late format-string reconstruction reach ordinary application code, the parser boundary failed.

Design implication: move from bags to types. Prefer repr-transparent newtypes with ZST/PhantomData markers, sealed traits, const generics, and parser-owned operation/result enums where they make invalid states unrepresentable: channel roles, family/model capability, parser state, frame length, payload length, selector/page id, tag/opcode, counters, telemetry units, verification/provenance, and presentation state. Implementation rule: start TDD-first, add property tests for parser/framer/state-machine behavior, use mutation tests where they add signal, keep hot ingest paths zero-allocation unless the alternative harms maintainability, and delete legacy raw/primitive/stringly compatibility paths aggressively. title: Make Veteran/Aero frame reassembly return ingest outcomes
description:

title: Migrate non-Aero protocol families onto ingest outcomes
description: Migrate Begode/Falcon and VESC/Refloat so their notification/reply ingest follows the same parser-first typed outcome model. Each family parser must turn bytes immediately into typed domain events, typed buffered progress, typed diagnostics, typed reserved evidence, or typed parser gaps. Do not leave family-specific raw-notification semantics or transport hacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Begode/Falcon and VESC/Refloat parsers emit the same parser-first typed outcome model as Veteran/Aero: semantic events, buffered/incomplete progress, diagnostics, known-reserved evidence, parser gaps, and ignored/wrong-channel outcomes.
2. Family parsers own raw bytes and use typed parser substrate/operation results before BTLE/dashboard/replay/mobile code sees data.
3. Add family-specific newtypes/traits for fixed-frame tags, sub-indexes, selectors, lengths, units, board/model capabilities, and verification state where they prevent confusion.
4. Tests cover hardware/source-backed expectations, fragmentation where applicable, malformed frames, reserved/gap evidence, and no raw notification fallback.
5. Delete family-specific primitive readers/raw-event compatibility paths; keep hot paths zero-allocation or explicitly justified.
notes:
Update after epic correction: this is not just adding NotificationIngestOutcome wrappers around existing frame parsers. For each family, parser/framer internals own raw bytes; output must be typed evidence/domain values before data reaches BTLE/dashboard/replay/mobile. If Begode or VESC needs new evidence newtypes, add them in core/protocol rather than carrying primitive bags or strings upward.

Standing constraints: TDD-first with comprehensive behavioral coverage; property tests for fragmentation/coalescing/state machines where useful; mutation tests where they add signal; no source-scanning tests; aggressively delete legacy family-specific raw event paths and compatibility shims; if a migration/refactor is larger than this issue, create/update child issues before continuing; preserve no-allocation/bounded hot paths unless avoiding allocation makes the model meaningfully worse; design family/model traits and evidence types for thousands of devices.

Threat model update 2026-06-23: treat BTLE protocol bytes like untrusted user input. Raw bytes enter transport/capture and parser internals only; after the first protocol boundary, normal session/report/dashboard/replay/mobile code should only see typed parser results, typed evidence, and typed domain events. If raw bytes, uuid/service/len strings, primitive selector/tag/body_len/event_count bags, or late format-string reconstruction reach ordinary application code, the parser boundary failed.

Design implication: move from bags to types. Prefer repr-transparent newtypes with ZST/PhantomData markers, sealed traits, const generics, and parser-owned operation/result enums where they make invalid states unrepresentable: channel roles, family/model capability, parser state, frame length, payload length, selector/page id, tag/opcode, counters, telemetry units, verification/provenance, and presentation state. Raw access is allowed only through explicit capture/provenance/debug artifacts with bounded metadata.

Implementation rule: start TDD-first, add property tests for parser/framer/state-machine behavior, use mutation tests where they add signal, keep hot ingest paths zero-allocation unless the alternative harms maintainability, and delete legacy raw/primitive/stringly compatibility paths aggressively. If the typed boundary work gets bigger than the issue in hand, create/update child issues rather than layering around weak shapes.
close_reason: Completed by the Begode/Falcon and VESC/Refloat parser/session migrations in the preceding protocol commits. Begode fixed-frame ingest now uses BegodeFrameParseResult::{Seeking, Buffered, Complete}, typed ByteCursor/ByteOffset readers, typed tag/page/evidence values, and emits NotificationIngestOutcome semantic/buffered/diagnostic paths from the session without raw-notification fallback or output Vec length inference. VESC stream ingest now uses VescReadOnlyStreamResult::{Buffered, Replies}, maps complete replies into typed telemetry/read-only/diagnostic domain events, reports buffered and parser diagnostic outcomes distinctly, and computes semantic event counts from reply semantics. Raw family bytes remain inside parser/framer internals and explicit capture/provenance artifacts; BTLE/dashboard/replay/mobile consume typed outcomes/evidence/domain values. Family tests cover Begode fragmentation/coalescing/malformed frames, typed parser progress/complete results, source-backed telemetry/BMS expectations, VESC complete/chunked/one-byte stream decoding, typed buffered/reply stream results, and no raw semantic transport logging through existing BTLE/session coverage. Hot paths remain bounded/zero-allocation, with inline parser result variants used deliberately. title: Design scheduler fairness and priority policy
description:
Implement the first deterministic scheduler policy layer on top of RequestQueue. Knowledge from cutout-4b3: RequestQueue is intentionally FIFO, bounded, duplicate-key checked, allocation-free, and protocol-agnostic. Fairness/priority should therefore be represented as explicit request metadata and queue insertion policy, not hidden inside protocol sessions or RequestTracker.

Scope for this slice: add transport-independent request urgency metadata and bounded priority insertion behavior for queued read-only work. The core policy should prefer urgent safety/identity probes ahead of routine telemetry, preserve FIFO order within the same urgency, refuse duplicate keys, and fail closed on capacity. Keep this synchronous, const-generic, no async/BLE/platform/serde/file IO, and no source-scanning tests.

Non-scope: protocol-specific poll cadence, dynamic starvation aging, safe-control arming, and actual BLE action generation. Add or link beads issues for those rather than skipping them.

Acceptance: failing tests first for higher-urgency insertion, same-urgency FIFO preservation, duplicate refusal before/after priority decisions, full-queue behavior, and property-tested monotonic urgency ordering. Validation uses nix develop with focused tests, fmt, check, clippy, workspace tests, and cargo-deny. Miri remains skipped for now and tracked by cutout-dly.
close_reason: Implemented the first static scheduler priority layer in cutout-core. Added RequestUrgency metadata, routine default construction, explicit with_urgency construction, and enqueue_by_urgency for bounded priority insertion while preserving FIFO within the same urgency and refusing duplicates/full queues before reordering. Added TDD coverage for urgency insertion, same-urgency FIFO, duplicate/full behavior, and property-tested monotonic urgency order. Created follow-up issues cutout-core-reactor-domain-model-lkk.8 for starvation aging and cutout-core-reactor-domain-model-lkk.7 for scheduler diagnostics. Validation: nix develop -c cargo test -p cutout-core request_queue; cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo check --workspace; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo deny check. Miri skipped per current project decision and tracked by cutout-dly.

Implement the Refloat package extension over COMM_CUSTOM_APP_DATA command ID 36, package interface ID 101, command INFO ID 0. Capture package name, semantic version, Git hash, tick rate, protocol version, and capability flags.

Acceptance: extension discovery is optional and failure leaves generic VESC read-only telemetry usable.
notes:
Boundary update: Refloat INFO runs over VESC custom-app traffic, but the public model should be namespaced libcutout Refloat extension structs with bounded strings/arrays. Do not leak generic raw custom-app payload bytes or vesc-rs command/reply enums through the public API. Optional Refloat INFO failure must leave generic VESC read-only telemetry usable.

title: Refloat live acceptance: capture, stream, replay
description:
Run the Refloat acceptance path after generic VESC and package support: connect, identify firmware, identify Refloat package, discover realtime IDs, stream realtime data, capture, replay, and compare events.

Acceptance: recorded, one-byte replay, and arbitrary-chunk replay produce equivalent semantic events.
notes:
Capture label taxonomy applies to Refloat live acceptance too. Use PEVCAP annotations capture_label=<slug>; minimum labels for a read-only acceptance matrix should include powered_on_stationary, rolling_forward or lifted_wheel if safe, disconnect_reconnect, and power_cycle. Charging and bms_screen are optional only if the board/app exposes relevant state. Replay acceptance should record which labels satisfy live, recorded, one-byte, and arbitrary-chunk equivalence.

title: Implement concrete UniFFI session wrappers outside core
description:
Build concrete, non-generic session wrapper types for mobile bindings in a crate that can depend on cutout-protocols. The wrapper surface should expose constructors such as NOSFET Aero read-only and Begode Falcon read-only without Rust generics, trait objects, borrowed buffers, async streams, or platform transport types crossing the FFI boundary. It should drive cutout-core HostSession through SessionInputDto::as_session_input and return owned SessionOutputDto values, snapshots, and diagnostics.

Acceptance: TDD-first tests construct each concrete wrapper, feed LinkUp/Notification/Tick/Command DTOs, drain owned output DTOs, query snapshot/diagnostics DTOs, and prove unsupported/profile-selection errors use explicit FFI result/error shapes. Generated Swift/Kotlin binding smoke checks are identified or implemented before closing. No source-scanning tests.
notes: Progress update: generated binding smoke-check planning is now explicit. docs/mobile-ffi.md records that current concrete wrappers are DTO-ready Rust APIs but the repo lacks a UniFFI component crate/export surface, cdylib/staticlib config, and generator/compiler commands. Follow-up work is split into cutout-z6t.1.3 for the UniFFI scaffold and cutout-z6t.1.4 for generated Swift/Kotlin compile smoke checks.
close_reason: Concrete mobile wrapper task is complete. cutout-protocols exposes concrete non-generic Aero and Falcon read-only wrappers, constructors, owned input/output/snapshot/diagnostic DTO flow, checked ingest result/error DTOs, and TDD coverage for LinkUp, Command, Notification, snapshots, diagnostics, unsupported commands, and unsupported profile construction. Generated Swift/Kotlin smoke checks are identified in docs/mobile-ffi.md and split into follow-ups cutout-z6t.1.3 and cutout-z6t.1.4 because the repo still needs an actual UniFFI component crate/export surface before generation can run. Acceptance: TDD-first tests prove unsupported command/refusal and constructor/profile failures are surfaced as stable owned DTO/error values, not panics, strings, Rust generics, trait objects, borrowed buffers, or platform transport types. No source-scanning tests.

title: Wire typed read-request encoders into read-only sessions
description:
ReadOnlySession currently subscribes and decodes notifications but ignores SessionInput::Command, so Falcon N/V request bytes cannot be exercised through the protocol session or CLI. Add a type-level request encoder hook for read-only model specs, using zero-sized model/encoder types and const/static dispatch rather than dynamic registries.

Acceptance: TDD-first protocol tests prove BegodeFalconModel RequestIdentity emits one WRITE_NO_RESPONSE payload 4e on BEGODE_DATA_CHANNEL, RequestFirmwareInfo emits 56, passive telemetry/battery requests emit no fake writes, unsupported diagnostics/control commands emit no writes, and NOSFET Aero behavior stays explicit. CLI hardware verification remains separate but can consume this path. No legacy compatibility layers or source-scanning tests.
notes: Implementation update: ReadOnlySession now has a type-level read-request encoder hook through SupportsReadRequests::Probe and encode_read_command. BegodeFalconModel maps RequestIdentity to WRITE_NO_RESPONSE payload 4e on BEGODE_DATA_CHANNEL and RequestFirmwareInfo to 56; telemetry/battery remain passive and diagnostics/control commands emit no writes. Tests cover the Falcon write/passive/unsupported behavior. Remaining hardware path work: CLI/session selection still needs to instantiate BegodeFalconModel after staged identity or via an explicit option before the real device verification issue can run end-to-end.
close_reason: Implemented typed read-request scheduling in ReadOnlySession: SupportsReadRequests now exposes a model-specific probe encoder, BegodeFalconModel emits N/V WRITE_NO_RESPONSE payloads on BEGODE_DATA_CHANNEL, passive telemetry/battery requests produce no writes, and unsupported diagnostics/control commands remain silent. Tests cover the Falcon write/passive/unsupported cases. CLI Falcon selection and real Bluetooth verification remain tracked separately.
